question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

-7680, -3840, -960, -480, -120, -60, ?, -7.5
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. -15.

GIVEN

• -7680, -3840, -960, -480, -120, -60, ?, -7.5

SOLUTION

• The terms are divided alternately by 2 and by 4.

• -7680 ÷2 = -3840; ÷4 = -960; ÷2 = -480; ÷4 = -120; ÷2 = -60.

• Next: -60 ÷4 = -15; then -15 ÷2 = -7.5 (matches the last term).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Watch the alternating operators ÷2, ÷4, ÷2, ÷4… The missing step is a ÷4, so -60 ÷4 = -15.

NOTE

• In division series always test constant ratios first, then alternating ratios (÷2/÷4) before trying differences.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

A, U, O, I, ?, W, Q, K
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. C.

GIVEN

• A, U, O, I, ?, W, Q, K

SOLUTION

• Take positions: A=1, U=21, O=15, I=9, ?, W=23, Q=17, K=11.

• Each letter moves -6 (mod 26): 1→21 (1-6=-5≡21), 21→15, 15→9, 9→3.

• So ? = position 3 = C (then 3-6=-3≡23=W, 23→17=Q, 17→11=K, all fit).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Constant step of -6 in the letter positions; 9 - 6 = 3 = C.

NOTE

• For letter series use A=1…Z=26 and treat wrap-arounds with mod 26 (0/negative → add 26).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

HP, ?, XD, SX, NR, IL, DF, YZ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. CJ.

GIVEN

• HP, ?, XD, SX, NR, IL, DF, YZ

SOLUTION

• First letters: H(8), ?, X(24), S(19), N(14), I(9), D(4), Y(25) → step -5 (mod 26): 8→3→24→19→14→9→4→25. So first letter = 3 = C.

• Second letters: P(16), ?, D(4), X(24), R(18), L(12), F(6), Z(26) → step -6 (mod 26): 16→10→4→24→18→12→6→26. So second letter = 10 = J.

• Missing term = CJ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Split into two columns; column-1 falls by 5, column-2 by 6. 8-5=3=C, 16-6=10=J.

NOTE

• Two-letter series are almost always two independent arithmetic sequences on positions.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and sixth letter cluster is related to fifth letter cluster.

FH : DC :: VG : ? :: QP : OK
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. TB.

GIVEN

• FH : DC :: VG : ? :: QP : OK

SOLUTION

• Pattern from FH→DC: F(6)-2=D(4), H(8)-5=C(3). Confirm with QP→OK: Q(17)-2=O(15), P(16)-5=K(11).

• Apply to VG: V(22)-2=T(20), G(7)-5=B(2) → TB.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter -2, second letter -5. V→T, G→B.

NOTE

• Verify the deduced rule on the third given pair (OK) before applying, to avoid trap options.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(GD, JG, NL)

(SZ, VC, ZH)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (LU, OX, SC).

GIVEN

• Reference sets: (GD, JG, NL) and (SZ, VC, ZH)

SOLUTION

• Rule (GD, JG, NL): first letters G(7)→J(10)→N(14) = +3,+4; second letters D(4)→G(7)→L(12) = +3,+5.

• Test (LU, OX, SC): first L(12)→O(15)→S(19) = +3,+4 ✓; second U(21)→X(24)→C(3, i.e. 29) = +3,+5 ✓.

• Other options fail (+6 jumps), so answer = (LU, OX, SC).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Check only the first letters of each cluster: needed pattern is +3 then +4. Only LU,OX,SC gives 12,15,19.

NOTE

• In 'find similar group' items, decode the increment pattern of positions and match it across options.

question: What will be the sum of the number of Tuesdays in the month of December of 2011 and March of 2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 8.

GIVEN

• Count Tuesdays in December 2011 and March 2012, then add.

SOLUTION

• 1 December 2011 = Thursday, so Tuesdays fall on 6, 13, 20, 27 → 4 Tuesdays.

• 1 March 2012 = Thursday, so Tuesdays fall on 6, 13, 20, 27 → 4 Tuesdays.

• Sum = 4 + 4 = 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month starting on Thursday puts Tuesday on the 6th → exactly 4 Tuesdays. Both months qualify → 4+4=8.

NOTE

• A weekday appears 5 times in a 31-day month only if the month starts on that day or the one/two before it; else 4 times.

question: If 4 March 2000 was Saturday, then what day was it on 4 August 2000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Friday.

GIVEN

• 4 March 2000 = Saturday. Find the day on 4 August 2000.

SOLUTION

• Days from 4 Mar to 4 Aug = Mar 31 + Apr 30 + May 31 + Jun 30 + Jul 31 = 153 days.

• 153 ÷ 7 gives remainder 6 (odd days).

• Saturday + 6 = Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Add month lengths between the two dates, take mod 7 (=6), then count forward 6 days from Saturday → Friday.

NOTE

• 'Odd days' = remainder when total days are divided by 7; add them to the known weekday.

question: 5 persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Only one person is sitting between C and D, while considering towards right of D. B is sitting second to the left of D. A is sitting to the immediate right of B. Who are the immediate neighbours of C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. B and E.

GIVEN

• 5 persons around a circle facing centre; one person between C and D (going right of D); B second to left of D; A immediate right of B.

SOLUTION

• Facing centre: left = clockwise, right = anticlockwise.

• Fix D. Second to left (clockwise) of D = B; immediate right (anticlockwise) of B = A, so order clockwise is D, A, B.

• Going right (anticlockwise) of D, one person then C: that person is E, then C. Clockwise seating: D, A, B, C, E.

• Neighbours of C = B and E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Lock D, A, B first (given directly), then the last two seats take E and C so C's neighbours are B and E.

NOTE

• For 'facing centre' circles, treat left as clockwise and right as anticlockwise consistently.

question: 7 girls P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). R is to the immediate right of S. Q is at one of the extreme ends of row. T is the immediate neighbour of Q. Only V is sitting between T and U. U is third to the right of P. How many girls are sitting between P and R?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1.

GIVEN

• Row of 7 facing north; R immediate right of S; Q at an end; T neighbour of Q; only V between T and U; U third to right of P.

SOLUTION

• Facing north, right = east (higher position). Put Q at the right end (7); T neighbour = 6.

• Only V between T and U → U(4) V(5) T(6). U third right of P → P = 1.

• Remaining seats 2,3 take S,R with R immediate right of S → S=2, R=3.

• Order: P, S, R, U, V, T, Q. Between P(1) and R(3) sits only S → 1 girl.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Anchor Q at the end, build T–V–U leftward, force P at seat 1; only S falls between P and R.

NOTE

• For north-facing rows, a person's right is your right when the row is drawn left-to-right as west-to-east.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

LO90 : NS30 :: AX70 : CB10 :: TP80 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. VT20.

GIVEN

• LO90 : NS30 :: AX70 : CB10 :: TP80 : ?

SOLUTION

• Letters: +2 on first, +4 on second. L(12)→N(14), O(15)→S(19); check A→C, X→B(28); numbers -60: 90→30, 70→10.

• Apply to TP80: T(20)→V(22), P(16)→T(20), 80-60=20 → VT20.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Rule = (+2, +4, -60). TP80 → VT20.

NOTE

• Treat the number as a whole (per the note); here simply subtract 60.

question:
Select the option that is related to the sixth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and third letter-number cluster is related to fourth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

PL120 : IQ220 :: ZK130 : SP230 :: ? : KK350
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. RF250.

GIVEN

• PL120 : IQ220 :: ZK130 : SP230 :: ? : KK350

SOLUTION

• Rule (first→second): first letter -7, second letter +5, number +100. Check: P(16)→I(9), L(12)→Q(17), 120→220; Z(26)→S(19), K(11)→P(16), 130→230.

• Sixth = KK350, so fifth (?) reverses it: K(11)+7=R(18), K(11)-5=F(6), 350-100=250 → RF250.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the (-7,+5,+100) rule on KK350: +7,-5,-100 → RF250.

NOTE

• When the unknown is the first of a pair, invert the derived rule.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

1804 : 1842 :: ? : 6101 :: 5862 : 5900
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 6063.

GIVEN

• 1804 : 1842 :: ? : 6101 :: 5862 : 5900

SOLUTION

• Relation: second = first + 38. Check 1804+38=1842 and 5862+38=5900.

• Here ? + 38 = 6101 → ? = 6101 - 38 = 6063.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference is constant +38; subtract 38 from 6101 → 6063.

NOTE

• Operate on whole numbers only (per the note); find the fixed additive gap first.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

96 : 32 :: 123 : 41 :: 246 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 82.

GIVEN

• 96 : 32 :: 123 : 41 :: 246 : ?

SOLUTION

• Relation: second = first ÷ 3. Check 96÷3=32, 123÷3=41.

• So 246 ÷ 3 = 82.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Each result is one-third of the given number; 246/3 = 82.

NOTE

• Test simple ratios (÷2, ÷3, ×2) on whole numbers before differences.

question: In a certain code language, 'advertisement create attraction' is coded as 'pq sm zp' and 'famous brands not need advertisement' is coded as 'zp la ta ro rq'. How will 'advertisement' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. zp.

GIVEN

• 'advertisement create attraction' = 'pq sm zp'

• 'famous brands not need advertisement' = 'zp la ta ro rq'

SOLUTION

• The only common word in both sentences is 'advertisement'.

• The only common code in both is 'zp'.

• Hence 'advertisement' = zp.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Match the common word to the common code word directly.

NOTE

• In message-coding, a word shared by two sentences maps to the code shared by them.

question: In a certain code language, 'TREES' is coded as '68' and 'START' is coded as '57'. How will 'BEAR' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 82.

GIVEN

• TREES = 68, START = 57. Find BEAR.

SOLUTION

• Use reverse alphabet values (A=26, B=25 … Z=1).

• TREES = T(7)+R(9)+E(22)+E(22)+S(8) = 68 ✓; START = S(8)+T(7)+A(26)+R(9)+T(7) = 57 ✓.

• BEAR = B(25)+E(22)+A(26)+R(9) = 82.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse value = 27 - normal position. Sum reverse values of the letters.

NOTE

• When forward-position sums fail, try reverse positions (A=26…Z=1).

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

TC201, ZK203, DQ205, IX207, NE209, SL211
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ZK203.

GIVEN

• TC201, ZK203, DQ205, IX207, NE209, SL211

SOLUTION

• First letters should step +5: T(20), Y(25), D(30=4), I(9), N(14), S(19). The 2nd term's first letter should be Y, not Z.

• Second letters should step +7: C(3), J(10), Q(17), X(24), E(31=5), L(38=12). The 2nd term's second letter should be J, not K.

• Numbers 201,203,205… (+2) are fine. So the 2nd term should be YJ203; the wrong term is ZK203.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Check first letters: T,_,D,I,N,S is 20,25,4,9,14,19 (+5). Y is expected, so ZK203 breaks it.

NOTE

• In 'find the wrong term', confirm the pattern using the terms that agree, then flag the outlier.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

SNE200, UPG357, WRI514, ?, AVM828
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. YTK671.

GIVEN

• SNE200, UPG357, WRI514, ?, AVM828

SOLUTION

• First letters +2: S(19), U(21), W(23), Y(25), A(27=1). Missing first = Y.

• Second letters +2: N(14), P(16), R(18), T(20), V(22). Missing second = T.

• Third letters +2: E(5), G(7), I(9), K(11), M(13). Missing third = K.

• Numbers +157: 200, 357, 514, 671, 828. Missing = 671 → YTK671.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Each letter +2, number +157. Fill between WRI514 and AVM828 → YTK671.

NOTE

• Break letter-number clusters into independent columns and progress each separately.

question: In 24 hours, how many times minute and hour hands of a clock will be opposite to each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 22.

GIVEN

• Count how many times the hands are opposite (180° apart) in 24 hours.

SOLUTION

• In 12 hours the hands are exactly opposite 11 times.

• In 24 hours = 2 × 11 = 22 times.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Hands coincide 11 times / 12 hr and are opposite 11 times / 12 hr → 22 times in a day.

NOTE

• In 12 hours: coincide 11, opposite 11, right angle 22 times.

question: The ratio of present ages of P and Q is 2 : 7. P is 5 years younger than Q. What is the present age of Q?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 7 years.

GIVEN

• P : Q = 2 : 7 and Q - P = 5 years.

SOLUTION

• Let P = 2x, Q = 7x. Then 7x - 2x = 5x = 5 → x = 1.

• Q = 7x = 7 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Difference of ratio parts = 7 - 2 = 5 parts = 5 years → 1 part = 1 year, so Q = 7.

NOTE

• Age-ratio problems: map the given difference onto the difference of ratio parts to get the unit value.

question: Sum of the present ages of J, P and S is 80 years. 10 years ago from the present the ratio of ages of J, P and S was 3 : 5 : 2. What is the present age of P?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 35 years.

GIVEN

• J + P + S = 80 now; 10 years ago J : P : S = 3 : 5 : 2.

SOLUTION

• Sum 10 years ago = 80 - (3×10) = 50 years.

• Ratio parts = 3+5+2 = 10, so 1 part = 50/10 = 5.

• P 10 years ago = 5×5 = 25; present P = 25 + 10 = 35 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Subtract 3×10=30 from 80 to get past sum 50; P = 5/10 × 50 + 10 = 35.

NOTE

• For 'N years ago' with three people, reduce today's sum by 3N to get the past sum, then split by ratio.
